oera.name: O.E.R.A.
oera.blurb: Oceanic Exploration and Research Alliance. Your employer.

civil.name: Civil Harbour Authority
civil.blurb: Public ports, coast guards and pilots.

pleasure.name: Private Yachts
pleasure.blurb: Owners with more money than seamanship.

cargo.name: Atlantic Freight Lines
cargo.blurb: Container ships and tankers on the lanes. Big, slow, and hard to stop.

fishing.name: North Atlantic Fleet Cooperative
fishing.blurb: Trawlers and longliners. Honest work until a quota gets tight.

foreign.name: Concord Naval Command
foreign.blurb: A foreign navy that does not like uninvited submarines near its listening posts.

deepcut.name: Deepcut Mining Consortium
deepcut.blurb: Nodule miners. Blunt, well funded, short on patience for inspections.

abyssal.name: Abyssal Metals Cooperative
abyssal.blurb: Vent sulphide miners on the Ridge. A workers' co-op with a safety record it is proud of.

ridgeline.name: Ridgeline Extraction Ltd
ridgeline.blurb: Cuts corners and claims. Their ships do not always answer hails.

meridian.name: Meridian Free Colony
meridian.blurb: Independent deep-water settlers. Polite, proud, short of supplies.

poachers.name: Grey Net Fleet
poachers.blurb: Illegal fishers in protected waters. They cut their nets and run.

pirates.name: Black Tide Syndicate
pirates.blurb: Raiders who hit miners and lone ships. Some fight, some flee, depending on the captain.

note: boldness: 0 = runs at the first sign of trouble, 1 = fights to the end. Each hostile vessel rolls its own value in this range.
